text:
priya: quick heads-up — onboarding mpt-7b-quant on staging: streaming responses sometimes terminate early when using our chat template. repro consistently with the sample below.

alex: saw a spike in 5xxs earlier, is this the same? can you drop logs? :eyes:

priya: yes same pattern. minimal repro (staging, quantized run):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"mpt-7b-quant","input":"User: write a one-paragraph story\nAssistant:","stream":true,"stop":["\u003c|endoftext|\u003e"]}'
```
Then the stream closes after a short phrase. Not a network timeout — the server emits an EOS and stream ends.

alex: can you paste the raw token stream (ids) around the stop?

priya: got a dump from the infer node: 
```
... 5021, 5021, 2, 5021, 5021, 5020, 1, 5021, 5021, 5020, 5020, ...
```
We see repeated sentinel ids (5021/5020). The tokenizer config has both `eos_token` and a `pad` alias in special_tokens, plus our chat template inserts "\u003c|endoftext|\u003e" and also a trailing explicit stop sequence — so overlap.

sasha: interesting — sounds like multi-token EOS (HF tokenizer) got split differently after quantization kernel reorder. config.json snippet attached from the model folder: 
```json
{"tokenizer_class":"MPTTokenizer","special_tokens_map":{"eos_token":"","additional_special_tokens":["\u003c|endoftext|\u003e","\u003c|sep|\u003e"]},"model_type":"mpt"}
```
chat template: "{{user}}\nAssistant:" + "\u003c|endoftext|\u003e" (we appended canonical sentinel). That double-def seems to create a race where the runtime emits one EOS then another micro-step emits a second EOS which our streaming stop handler treats as immediate stop — but sometimes the decoder emits a split EOS (two tokens) and the handler stops at the first piece, causing truncated output.

bench-bot: eval snapshot for the failing set (run 2026-03-19 14:02 UTC):
- throughput: 220 tok/s
- avg latency to first token: 80ms
- early_stop_rate (failing set): 12%
- median generated length (expected): 120 tok vs actual: 18 tok

devon: quick mitigation ideas: map all variants of special tokens to a single canonical eos id in the tokenizer preproc; or change streaming stop logic to wait for the full EOS token sequence (i.e., match tokens, not chars). Also add a small debounce window: if EOS arrives but previous token was part of a multi-token eos sequence, don't cut until we confirm token boundary.

alex: +1 on token-level matching. For quantized runs we saw tokenization alignment shifts (subword merges) so string-level stop checks are brittle.

priya: agreed. i'll open ENG-ML ticket with failing sample and logs. plan:
1) add token-level stop matcher to runtime (match sequence of token ids)
2) add a canary eval for multi-token eos cases in the onboarding harness
3) in the short term, normalize special_tokens_map to a single eos token in the HF->Redwood conversion step.

sasha: FYI we already have a converter step that rewrites `special_tokens_map` but it didn't catch `additional_special_tokens` used by templates. i'll push a converter patch to collapse duplicates.

bench-bot: queued a comparison run: `bench cmp --tag=quant-eos-fix --base=2026-03-18T` — will post diff when done.

devon: also adding these checks to `redwood/tests/onboarding_regressions/eos_cases.py` — test will assert no early stop on a set of synthetic multi-eos prompts.

priya: thanks all — assigning to sasha for converter, devon for runtime change, alex to review the canary. i'll attach the failing json and token dumps to the ticket. :thumbsup:
